caption: Imagine, many still believe the ‘official’ story…🙄
audio_track_actual: Interview audio: a host recounts William Rodriguez's 9/11 morning in the second person ('you're the janitor…') while Rodriguez confirms and elaborates. No music bed; word-tracking subtitle overlays.
video_overlay_text_observed: Split layout: two webcam interview frames up top (interviewer and guest), and the reel creator at the bottom wearing a tin-foil hat — a self-aware 'conspiracy' reaction framing. Overlay text 'IMAGINE THIS WASN'T WHAT WE HEARD IN THE NEWS…' and 'IT'S 9 11,' with a '@paulotik0tok' watermark.
audio_content_summary: The William Rodriguez account. The North Tower janitor — punched in at 8:30, working sub-level 1 of six sub-basements — says that at 8:46 he heard and felt an explosion from beneath him, big enough to lift him and others upward, a few seconds before a second blast from above that 'turned out [to be] the plane.' He insists 'there was definitely an explosion before the first plane,' says other basement witnesses would confirm it, and that he gave the 9/11 Commission a list of those eyewitnesses but his testimony 'doesn't show anywhere' in the report. He notes he held one of the master keys ('one of five pastries' is a transcription error) granting access to all doors in the complex, and that he tells the story in a motivational speech worldwide, aired unedited only by C-SPAN.
implied_frame: Group A / Group B, carded at 2001-rodriguez-001. Verifiable: Rodriguez was a real North Tower maintenance worker with a master key, decorated for heroism in the evacuation, who met the 9/11 Commission behind closed doors; his account is absent from the final report. Contested: the sub-basement explosion 'before the plane,' which is the load-bearing claim for the controlled-demolition reading. The both-sides hinge is in the record — Rodriguez's own account of a fireball racing down the elevator shaft (which burned co-worker Felipe David) matches the mainstream mechanism for basement damage: jet fuel descending the shafts from the impact above, not a pre-planted charge. The pre-impact timing is what the official timeline and NIST do not support. The reel's '576 pages' is a near-miss on the report's 567.
